issues.legal_issue: The correspondence between the government engineer and the applicant formed a concluded agreement to supply canal water for the specified cane cultivation.
material_facts: The Superintending Engineer, acting on instructions from the Public Works Minister, wrote that the applicant could concentrate cane irrigation in a defined area and continue it permanently if he chose, subject to taking measured water and paying the rates set by the government.
The Superintending Engineer communicated those terms to the applicant, who accepted them.
The applicant thereafter concentrated his holdings in the area and received water on the agreed basis.
issues.conclusion: The documents recorded a concluded agreement to supply water so long as the applicant had cane cultivation in the concentrated area.
issues.legal_principle: The documents must be read together and in light of their terms and context. Permission to cultivate cane permanently on the stated basis necessarily implied continuing water supply, because cane cultivation and canal-water supply were inseparably connected.

rule.if: civil_appeal_concerning_water_supply_agreement and official_communicated_agreed_terms and applicant_accepted_terms and conduct_followed_arrangement

predicates.civil_appeal_concerning_water_supply_agr: The matter is a civil appeal concerning an alleged agreement for water supply.
predicates.official_communicated_agreed_terms: A government official communicated settled water-supply terms to the applicant.
predicates.applicant_accepted_terms: The applicant accepted the communicated terms.
predicates.conduct_followed_arrangement: The applicant reorganized the relevant activity as contemplated by the arrangement and received water on that basis.

issues.definition: When a civil appeal concerning a water-supply agreement involves communicated and accepted terms followed by conduct consistent with them, the output is that the agreement was concluded.

issues.legal_issue: A canal-water supply agreement made through the statutory application process is presumed to pass with the land when the land is transferred.
material_facts: The applicant became the owner of the land and sought recognition of the associated right to use canal water.
The court explained that the irrigation statute provided for applications to a canal officer and for a presumption that an agreement for water supply to land transferred with that land.
The particular agreement in this case was found to have been made outside that statutory scheme.
issues.conclusion: An agreement for canal-water supply to land is presumed to transfer with the land, although that statutory rule did not govern the agreement in this case because it was made outside the statutory scheme.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 27 and 30 of the Bombay Irrigation Act, 1879, a person seeking canal water applies to a canal officer, and an agreement for water supply to land is presumed transferred when the land is transferred. The separate restriction on transferring a water-use right without permission does not displace that presumption for an agreement transferred with land.

predicates.statutory_water_supply_agreement: The water-supply agreement was made through the statutory process for obtaining canal water.
predicates.land_transferred: The land to which the water-supply agreement relates was transferred to another person.

issues.definition: When a statutory water-supply agreement relates to land that is transferred, the output is that the agreement is presumed to pass with the land.

issues.legal_issue: The agreement was made outside the statutory canal-water supply scheme rather than under that scheme.
material_facts: The application seeking continued water supply and exclusion of the applicant’s land from a proposed factory area was considered by the government and the relevant minister.
The Superintending Engineer communicated the arrangement on ministerial instructions.
The statutory scheme provided for applications to an empowered canal officer but did not provide a process for seeking exclusion from a factory area and permanent supply on the terms arranged.
The parties later exchanged drafts of a formal agreement, and they also made yearly applications under the statutory scheme for water supply.
issues.conclusion: The agreement was made between the government and the applicant outside the provisions of the Bombay Irrigation Act, 1879.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 3(6), 4, and 27–30 of the Bombay Irrigation Act, 1879, and the rules made under it provide for applications and permissions for canal-water supply, including the statutory consequences of agreements made through that scheme. They do not provide for the type of application and government arrangement made here.

predicates.water_arrangement_case: The dispute concerns an arrangement for canal-water supply.
predicates.application_bypassed_statutory_process: The applicant sought the arrangement through a process not provided for in the statutory water-supply scheme.
predicates.government_minister_set_terms: Government officials and a minister considered the request and set the arrangement’s terms.

issues.definition: When a water arrangement is sought outside the statutory process and its terms are set through a government ministerial arrangement, the output is that the agreement was made outside the statutory scheme.

issues.legal_issue: A government contract made in the exercise of provincial executive authority is void if it is not expressed to be made by the Governor or is not executed by a person authorized to act on the Governor’s behalf.
material_facts: The water-supply arrangement was made between the government and the applicant outside the irrigation statute and therefore in the exercise of provincial executive authority.
The documents did not express the contract to be made in the Governor’s name.
The record did not establish that the Superintending Engineer was legally authorized to enter into that contract on the government’s behalf.
issues.conclusion: The agreement was void because it neither complied with the required form of expression nor was shown to have been executed by an authorized person.
issues.legal_principle: Section 175(3) of the Government of India Act, 1935, required contracts made in the exercise of a Province’s executive authority to be expressed as made by the Governor and executed on the Governor’s behalf by a person and in a manner authorized by the Governor. The provision is mandatory. Seth Bikhraj Jaipuria v. Union of India and New Marine Coal Co. v. Union of India held that contracts not meeting these requirements are void. Union of India v. Rallia Ram permits the requirements to be assessed by a fair reading of the documents, but does not dispense with them.

rule.if: civil_appeal_concerning_state_contract and executive_authority_contract and (not expressed_in_governor_name or not executed_by_authorized_person)

predicates.civil_appeal_concerning_state_contract: The matter is a civil appeal concerning a contract made by the government.
predicates.executive_authority_contract: The contract was made in the exercise of the government’s executive authority.
predicates.expressed_in_governor_name: The contract was expressed to be made in the Governor’s name.
predicates.executed_by_authorized_person: The contract was executed on the Governor’s behalf by a person authorized to do so.

issues.definition: When a civil appeal concerns a government contract made under executive authority and either required formality is absent, the output is that the contract is void.
